{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Marion Kirkland "Kirk" Fort Jr.''' (1921–1964) was an American [[mathematician]], specializing in [[general topology]]. The [[topological space]]s called [[Fort space]] and [[Arens–Fort space]] are named after him.

Fort was born in 1921 in [[Spartanburg, South Carolina]], where he graduated with an [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] from [[Wofford College]] in 1941. He received an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in 1944 from the [[University of Virginia]], where he also received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1948, advised by [[Gordon Thomas Whyburn]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=505|title=Marion Kirk Fort Jr.}}</ref> He was at the [[University of Illinois]] from then until 1953, when he came to the [[University of Georgia]] (UGA). He later served as head of the UGA mathematics department, 1959&ndash;1963. In 1963 Fort became the first holder of the university's [[David C. Barrow]] Chair of Mathematics. He died in 1964 during a [[leave of absence]] at the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Department of Mathematics History | url = http://www.math.uga.edu/about_us/history.html | work = Department of Mathematics | publisher = University of Georgia | accessdate = February 15, 2008 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20080209161759/http://www.math.uga.edu/about_us/history.html | archivedate = February 9, 2008 }}</ref>
